item.title: A Tough Week for Crypto Has Fans Downing Drinks at a Bitcoin Bar
item.description: It was a tough week for crypto, but a good time to get a drink by Thursday evening.

item.title: Singapore to Ensure AI Helps Workers Worried About Jobs, PM Says
item.description: Singapore is benefitting from the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and the government is making use of the technology to ensure higher productivity and better jobs for workers who are worried about their livelihoods, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said.

item.title: How AI Is Triggering a Surge in American Imports: New Economy
item.description: Deep-pocketed tech firms racing to build data centers have largely gotten a pass from Trump’s protectionism.

item.title: World Economy Latest: US Employment Declines Unexpectedly
item.description: A surprise drop in US payrolls renewed worries about the job market in the world’s largest economy, suggesting employers are growing cautious amid rising prices and fallout from the Iran war.

item.title: Zimbabwe to Cap Gold-Buying Support at $300 Million This Year
item.description: Zimbabwe said it will cap government support for buying gold at $300 million this year and review the scheme in the 2027 national budget, according to a letter from top economic officials to the International Monetary Fund.

item.title: Zelenskyy Makes Debut Trip to Serbia as Russian Influence Wanes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is making a landmark first visit on Saturday to Serbia, the Balkan country whose leader has been scaling back once-close ties with Russia.

item.title: Kyiv Struck as Ukraine Targets Russian Refineries, Shadow Fleet
item.description: A fire was sparked at Russia’s Ilsky oil refinery in the southern Krasnodar region by Ukrainian drone debris, injuring five people, the regional task force said on Saturday, as Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight attacks including a large-scale missile barrage on Kyiv.

item.title: Burnham’s Fiscal ‘Flexibility’ Could Backfire, Officials Fear
item.description: UK Treasury officials are concerned that the prime minister’s talk of using “flexibility” within the fiscal rules to ramp up investment could backfire by destabilizing financial markets, according to people familiar with the thinking.

item.title: WuXi AppTec Gets Temporary Reprieve of Chinese Military Label
item.description: A US judge blocked the Defense Department from enforcing its designation of WuXi AppTec Co. as a Chinese military company, granting temporary relief to the major pharmaceutical contractor.

item.title: War Brings Winter of Discontent for the World’s Workhorse Fuel
item.description: A diesel squeeze spurred by wars in the Middle East and Ukraine is setting the stage for an even worse crunch as demand rises ahead of the Northern Hemisphere winter.

item.title: Situational Awareness’s Mystery Investment Was to Source Foundry
item.description: A mystery $400 million investment made by Situational Awareness just days after the hedge fund was on the brink of collapse was to chip manufacturing startup Source Foundry, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Union Workers Strike at BHP’s Port Hedland Iron Ore Export Hub
item.description: Unionized workers at BHP Group’s Port Hedland iron ore export hub in Western Australia have started rolling 24-hour strikes, escalating a pay dispute ahead of further meetings with the company.

item.title: Canada’s PSP Is Said to Mull $1.5 Billion Sale of Roads in India
item.description: The Public Sector Pension Investment Board is exploring options for its roads in India, including a sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: New Zealand Slaps New Sanctions Against Russia After US Move
item.description: New Zealand announced more sanctions targeting individuals and entities supporting Russia’s war against Ukraine, following the passage of a new bill in the US Senate targeting the country’s oil and gas revenues.

item.title: US Partly Resumes Operations in Mexico’s Avocado State Michoacan
item.description: The US will partially resume operations in Mexico’s top avocado-producing state, days after security concerns prompted a halt that disrupted inspections for exports.

item.title: SEC Drops Insider-Trading Suit Against Executive Trump Pardoned
item.description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission said it is dropping an insider-trading lawsuit against a former healthcare executive who was convicted in a related criminal case and then pardoned by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Data Center Firm Switch to File Confidentially for IPO
item.description: Switch Inc. filed confidentially for a US IPO, according to people familiar with the matter, joining its data center peers in tapping demand for exposure to the artificial intelligence theme.

item.title: SpaceX Nears IPO Price Again After Staging $327 Billion Rally
item.description: SpaceX shares jumped for a second straight day bringing them close to breaking back above the company’s $135 initial public offering price for the first time since falling below the key level last month.

item.title: SoftBank-Backed 3D Printer Maker Formlabs Is Said to Weigh IPO
item.description: Formlabs, a maker of 3D printers, is in early talks with potential advisers for an initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Wall Street Risk Complex Surges Anew Amid Deluge of Fresh Cash
item.description: The financial world’s catalog of complaints keeps getting longer. In markets, however, the response is increasingly one of indifference.

item.title: Hedge Funds Slashed Yen Short Bets After US-Japan Joint Efforts
item.description: Hedge funds sharply reduced bearish bets on the yen after coordinated efforts by US and Japanese officials helped stabilize the currency.

item.title: Fed Split on Rate Hikes Deepens as High Inflation Tests Patience
item.description: Five years of high inflation is testing the patience of Federal Reserve officials and showcasing a split between those willing to wait before hiking interest rates and those who say time is running out.

item.title: JPMorgan Boosts Tech Bond Sales Outlook as AI Debt Binge Expands
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. sees bond sales from technology-related firms exceeding half a trillion dollars this year, as hyperscalers’ appetite to deploy capital for the artificial intelligence buildout shows no sign of abating despite growing investor fatigue.

item.title: Brazil Treasury Seeks to Calm Fears of Foreign Bond Sales Surge
item.description: Brazil’s government is seeking flexibility rather than a wave of overseas bond sales as it asks Congress for authorization to issue as much as $35 billion a year in global markets, Treasury Secretary Daniel Leal said in an interview.

item.title: Phelan Confirmed to Lead Trump’s Council of Economic Advisers
item.description: The US Senate confirmed Christopher Phelan, a former adviser to the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, as chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers.

item.title: US Sanctions Iranian Digital Exchanges as Trump Promises Deal
item.description: The US ramped up economic pressure on Iran with more sanctions on digital asset exchanges and networks connected to the country’s shadow-banking system, as President Donald Trump says Washington and Tehran are coming close to an agreement.

item.title: US Treasury Sparks Debate Over Auction Cutbacks to Temper Yields
item.description: The US Treasury triggered debate this week about something that’s for years been an article of faith about the world’s biggest bond market: the government’s auctions of notes and bonds will just have to keep getting bigger.

item.title: DraftKings CEO Blasts Prediction Bets on Earnings Call Comments
item.description: DraftKings Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jason Robins said he doesn’t think it is good that bettors are placing prediction market wagers on what executives say on company earnings calls.

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Some Work on New Astra Model Over Cyber Concerns
item.description: OpenAI is pausing some internal work around one of its upcoming artificial intelligence models to implement stricter safeguards after the system was found to be significantly more adept at cybersecurity tasks.

item.title: Why Take-Two Won’t Share ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Pre-Order Numbers
item.description: CEO Strauss Zelnick says he doesn’t want to mislead shareholders
